learner_operation: Locate the main diagonal, inspect zeros on both sides, distinguish upper/lower/diagonal, and select the most specific supplied class. A witness may be anywhere on the permitted side.

fixed_features.feature: Square numeric matrix and direct classification
fixed_features.justification: Tutorial 658a47dc-4d32-5d9d-a04c-82d683e87739 defines triangularity for square matrices; observed questions require no transformations or arithmetic.

fixed_features.feature: One radio field with five full labels
fixed_features.justification: All eleven source questions supply this response bank; most-specific wording resolves class nesting.

fixed_features.feature: Normal classes upper, lower and nonidentity diagonal
fixed_features.justification: These are the three observed source families. Identity and Other are distractors here, not a promise to teach arbitrary matrix classification.

Observed easy source questions support both sizes and values through 10; conservative bounds retain the source workload. Eighteen support patterns are a finite classification family; number changes do not manufacture new structures.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Either upper or lower region can vanish; both can vanish for diagonal.
answer_roles.observed: All three classes occur at both easy sizes in the full-catalog sample. Exact batch has two lower, two upper, one diagonal, all 3x3.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Every nonempty subset of the permitted side; no fixed first witness or density threshold.
answer_roles.observed: All 18 easy supports appear; all six 3x3 sole-witness coordinates accepted, including far coordinates. Canonical accepted normally.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Diagonal values including zero, signs, nonzero magnitudes, A/C may change without changing zero support/class.
answer_roles.observed: Independent draws and controlled irrelevant changes preserve class; the batch rejection conditions joint cue collisions without forbidding any single parameter value.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Presentation order may vary independently of class.
answer_roles.observed: Raw correct positions vary. Actual UI reorders by task-item/field/choice IDs; fixed preview positions 5,2,4,3,4. Fixture-only later-orientation coincidence separately investigated.

coverage.case: All eligible easy structural patterns and sparse witnesses
coverage.result: 18/18 support patterns observed, with every 3x3 sole witness accepted.

coverage.case: Exact runner batch before/after rejection and delivery
coverage.result: Two rejected incidental redraws, then exact batch replayed; all five delivered without difficulty removal or deduplication.
Seeds 263,1227,40291 each yield five distinct structures with 2 lower,2 upper,1 diagonal; 15/15 survive delivery.

coverage.case: All original supported source cases and complete banks
coverage.result: 11 raw question replays pass; canonical normally accepted. Missing fields are preserved, not invented as source evidence.

counterfactuals.change: Transpose the canonical nonzero support with diagonal fixed; then clear that witness.
counterfactuals.expected: Lower changes to upper; clearing changes lower to diagonal.
counterfactuals.observed: Records 0/1/2 render lower/upper/diagonal matrices and matching conclusions; all five labels for each were native graded correctly.
counterfactuals.justification: Lesson definitions depend on which complete off-diagonal region vanishes, not a fixed source label.

counterfactuals.change: Change diagonal values and flip the sign of the sole nonzero, preserving support.
counterfactuals.expected: Lower remains lower, with updated printed matrix and witness.
counterfactuals.observed: Records 0/3 both classify lower; updated values and witness rendered correctly. Native grader accepts lower and rejects every distractor.
counterfactuals.justification: Tutorial explicitly permits any number, including zero, on the diagonal and permitted side. Only off-diagonal zero support matters.

shortcut_probes.strategy: 2x2 => diagonal; otherwise negative a11 => upper, nonnegative => lower
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline .2 is uniform guessing over five labels. Strict old rule has counterexamples; no longer a perfect predictor.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Best fitted label lookup per sign/letter group
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline .2 is uniform five-label guessing. Fitted resubstitution rate, not held-out prediction. Opposite orientations share cues, so the combined lookup leaves counterexamples.

Baseline .2 is uniform position guessing. Small single-template samples are descriptive; template class itself requires the intended mathematics. Raw order is independently reordered by actual UI task IDs. Exact UI examined separately.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Best fitted lookup from the three diagonal signs
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Uniform five-label baseline .2. Matching (-,-,-) diagonal signs occur in both lower and upper; (-,+,-) occurs in lower and diagonal. The cue cannot classify this pool.

shortcut_probes.strategy: Choose first among the upper/lower raw options
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline .5 chooses randomly between the two orientations after identifying non-diagonal triangular structure. First gets 1/4 and last 3/4; neither bypasses orientation on all raw records. Actual UI order is examined separately.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: exact batch in fixed preview fixture
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Uniform five-position baseline .2; preview positions [5,2,4,3,4] give at most 2/5. Live task IDs can change these positions.

shortcut_probes.subgroup: fixed preview content IDs 1..5: four triangular cases
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline .5 over two orientations. A 4/4 preview-fixture coincidence was investigated, not suppressed: exact UI choiceOrder depends on task-item ID. Each record yields both orders across IDs 100000..100127; native grading accepts the four preview actions and rejects four alternate-ID actions. No stable generator or actual delivered-cohort predictor established.

shortcut_probes.cue: later upper/lower option after diagonal detection
shortcut_probes.subgroup: same five records over 128 alternative task-ID seeds
shortcut_probes.strategy: If all off-diagonal entries are zero choose diagonal; otherwise choose later orientation
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Baseline .6 = one certainly recognized diagonal plus random orientation on four triangular records, averaged across five. The 405/640 rate has many failures. Uses exact extracted unmodified UI function, confirmed against rendered HTML; future real item IDs unknown.

shortcut_probes.cue: nonzero location relative to main diagonal
shortcut_probes.strategy: Inspect off-diagonal support and select the most specific class
shortcut_probes.conclusion: Uniform five-label baseline .2. This 5/5 rule IS the intended skill, because the lesson defines classes by those zero regions.

stages_examined: Difficulty-weighted learner selection and seen-prefix exclusion, read-only reproduction
delivery.result: No tested stable incidental predictor survives the current exact pool. 30/30 independent, 5/5 runner and 15/15 fresh records survive shared delivery. Actual selection rules leave every fresh easy member reachable under positive easy weight; both rank orders and seen-prefix exclusions tested.

limitations: Captured inventory basis 5451 may change after review. No database accessed or assets published.

Real future task-item IDs, numeric question entities, learner histories and policy weights are unavailable; selection and UI order were reproduced read-only with explicit synthetic IDs and scoped conclusions.
Fixed preview IDs create a later-orientation coincidence (4/4), but it is not invariant under actual UI task-ID ordering. No attributable stored generated cohort demonstrates this coincidence.

Sixteen inventory matrices inspected; 15 available keys agree. Missing generation/batch provenance prevents historical batch-shortcut incidence testing. Empty affected_questions is not a verified absence.
Finite tests cannot rule out every shortcut. No second exhaustive audit of unchanged 4x4 content was performed; requested easy and changed construction rules were tested.
